topic.title: Confidence Calibration and Predictive Uncertainty
topic.overview: Calibration asks whether a model's stated confidence matches how often its predictions are correct. This topic studies training losses, proper scoring rules, density-based uncertainty, ensembles, and post-training recalibration. A representative study investigates focal loss as a way to improve calibration during training, with temperature scaling providing an additional adjustment afterward.
topic.whyItMatters: Accuracy alone does not tell users when to rely on a prediction. Useful uncertainty must be both reliable and informative, supporting decisions such as abstention, comparison, or further inspection without merely making every prediction vague.
topic.evolution: The representatives range from probability forecasting to neural calibration and sharp uncertainty estimates. Recent work examines sample-dependent temperature scaling and uses uncertainty sets to question whether misclassification really demonstrates successful unlearning. These applications show how confidence evaluation can expose weaknesses hidden by ordinary accuracy metrics.
openQuestions: How stable is calibration under distribution changes?
Which uncertainty evaluations distinguish useful caution from uninformative predictions or superficial changes in model behavior?
